description: Things a project needs: materials, fittings, tools. The 'item list' — what has to be bought before work can happen. Import THIRTY-SEVENTH (needs user_projects)
notes: An item is a PLAN to spend, not a spend. What actually left the bank is an expense (38); keeping them apart is what lets a project show 'committed' and 'spent' as different numbers, which is the whole point of a budget.

project_id, task_id and milestone_id are TEXT holding row ids, not link_rows - same reasoning as everywhere else in this app: a link field cannot hold a client-generated id, and it makes every read fan out.
quantity and unit_cost are separate so '10 bags at 6.50' can be shown as it was decided. Total is derived, never stored: a stored total is a number that can disagree with its own parts.
unit is free text ('bags', 'm2', 'each'). A select would reject whatever the next job needs.
status is needed/ordered/have. 'ordered' matters because money is committed but nothing has arrived, and that is exactly when a plan looks finished and is not.
planned_for is when it should be bought, which is how the item plan sorts itself into stages without inventing another table.

title.description: What it is, e.g. '10 bags Quikrete'. Primary field

user_id.description: Xano user id as a string. EVERY read filters on this

task_id.description: Optional: the task that needs it

milestone_id.description: Optional: the stage it belongs to

quantity.description: How many. 1 when it does not matter

unit_cost.description: Cost of ONE. Total is quantity x this, derived

currency.description: ISO code. Blank means the project's own
